title: Pin the nested bun test inside bun run check to the declared bun, not PATH's
description: Local-tooling defect. package.json check chains test, whose final command is a BARE bun test. When bun run check is launched by an absolute-path bun (e.g. the declared /opt/homebrew/Cellar/bun/1.4.2/bin/bun), the nested bare bun test still resolves the bun on PATH, which on this workstation is 1.3.14. test/qcli411-bun-declare-binding.test.ts then fails with "bun 1.3.14 silently stripped a top-level binding named declare", so bun run check exits 1 on a clean tree. package.json declares packageManager bun@1.4.2, so a command meant to assert the declared runtime instead reddens because of an undeclared ambient one. CI passes because CI PATH bun is the pinned one, so this is a local-reproduction and review-evidence problem, not a CI one. Evidence: PR opum-ai/quest-cli#548 independent review (opum-workflow:review-assignment run wf_f04cfbbb-807, 2026-10-10). Its check-1 named /opt/homebrew/Cellar/bun/1.4.2/bin/bun run check exactly as written and measured exit 1 (1123 pass / 1 fail; the single failure is test/qcli411-bun-declare-binding.test.ts). Because a NAMED check failed, the review envelope outcome read findings while review.verdict was approve on a clean tree. Envelope sha256 883668e2b07049d0e80e6f0c9192524c501c09538bd6c973a4e482ce5746e762, recorded in opum-control against job-1mp405u at sha a84a3355848f3cc4996bbc41ed95958a488311d9. With PATH prefixed to the pinned bun the same tree exits 0. Fix direction is not prescribed here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Running the declared runtime by absolute path (e.g. /opt/homebrew/Cellar/bun/1.4.2/bin/bun run check) exits 0 on a clean tree even when the bun on PATH is a different version, because the nested test runner uses the declared bun rather than PATH's.
A check pins this, so the nested runner cannot silently fall back to PATH's bun again.
